html:
Mahmud of Ghazni was the Turkic ruler of the Ghaznavid state from 998 to 1030. From his capital at Ghazni, in today's Afghanistan, he built an empire from eastern Iran to the Punjab.

His father Sabuktigin had been a Turkic slave soldier who rose to govern Ghazni for the Samanids. Mahmud broke free of the fading Samanids and won the blessing of the Abbasid caliph. He is often said to be the first ruler to use the title sultan.

He led around seventeen raids into north India between about 1000 and 1027. He sacked rich temple cities such as Mathura and, in 1025, Somnath, carrying off vast treasure. In India he is remembered as a destroyer; in parts of the Muslim world, as a holy warrior.

His court was also a centre of Persian culture. He drew scholars and poets to Ghazni, among them the polymath al-Biruni. The poet Ferdowsi presented the Shahnameh to him; legend says Mahmud paid him poorly. Soon after his death the Seljuks took the west of his empire.
sum: Mahmud of Ghazni was the Turkic ruler of the Ghaznavid state from 998 to 1030. From his capital at Ghazni, in today's Afghanistan, he built an empire from eastern Iran to the Punjab.
